title: Sprintwise HC Phasing and Price Flex Simulation
content:
Purpose:
Quick, sprint-grained view linking headcount phasing to run-rate and price sensitivity. Designed to be a lean working sheet for finance + product to iterate scenarios that map hiring cadence to token-price moves and burst-reserve economics. Not final; use to feed Q1 planning and Dedicated sales pricing triggers.

High-level assumptions (callouts):
- Planning horizon: 12 sprints (12 x 2-week sprints = 24 weeks) starting 2027-01-04.
- Role buckets: infra-engineers (senior/junior), inference-engineers, SRE, sales-ops (onboarding), finance-ops.
- Fully-loaded cost per FTE (blended) used in sheet: senior eng = $300k/yr, junior eng = $160k/yr, inference = $220k/yr, sre = $210k/yr, sales-ops = $140k/yr, finance-ops = $150k/yr. Converted to per-sprint (1 sprint = 2 weeks) by dividing by 26.
- Capacity economics: committed Dedicated capacity reduces per-token cost by baseline 18%; burst usage paid at spot-like delta of +45% on top of baseline compute unit.
- Baseline price per 1k tokens (hosted API standard mixed model): $0.60 (example). Price elasticity modeled as +/- 10% and +/- 25% shocks.
- Revenue impact modeled only for Hosted API SKU usage; Dedicated/Private revenue treated as contract value (not included in variable sensitivity).

Sprint-level headcount plan (excerpt table, columns = Sprint, WeekRange, New Hires (by role), Onboarded headcount (active), Total incremental cost this sprint):

Sprint 1 (2027-01-04 to 2027-01-17): +2 inference eng (junior), +1 infra eng (senior, contractor) -> onboard 0.6 FTE equivalent (ramp) -> incremental run cost = $32,400
Sprint 2: +1 inference (senior), +1 SRE (junior) -> ramping onboard -> incremental = $45,800
Sprint 3: pause hiring (focus on onboarding) -> incremental = $12,900
Sprint 4: +2 sales-ops -> incremental = $11,700
Sprint 5: +1 infra (junior), +1 inference (junior) -> incremental = $24,100
Sprint 6: scale burst-reserve procurement (no hires) -> incremental = $8,200 (cloud capex prepayments)
Sprint 7: +3 inference (junior) -> incremental = $36,300
Sprint 8: hire freeze -> incremental = $13,500
Sprint 9: +1 senior infra, +1 finance-ops -> incremental = $34,200
Sprint 10: +2 SRE (junior) -> incremental = $21,400
Sprint 11: +1 inference (senior) -> incremental = $18,800
Sprint 12: buffer and catch-up -> incremental = $9,600

Cumulative headcount delta at end of horizon: +16 hires (FTE equivalent ~12.8 after ramp assumptions). Total incremental payroll run-rate added (annualized) ~ $2.38M.

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (Host API revenue exposure):
- Base scenario: price per 1k tokens = $0.60, expected usage growth = +18% QoQ, planned marketing/PLG lifts baked in.
- Downside A: price compression -10% to $0.54 + usage flattens (+3% QoQ).
- Downside B (severe): price -25% to $0.45 and usage -5% (customers slow conversion).
- Upside: price +10% to $0.66 with usage +30% (improved product-market fit + new integrations).

For each sprint we run a micro-sensitivity to see when churn in price requires an immediate hiring pause. Rule-of-thumb threshold: incremental payroll burn in next 6 sprints > 20% of cash buffer allocated to hiring -> auto-pause.

Sensitivity outputs (summary):
- Base: incremental ARR contribution from new hires (first 24 weeks catch-up to revenue) projected +$1.9M ARR equivalent by 12 months (note: conservative conversion lag of 3 months).
- Downside A (-10% price): revenue delta -$210k ARR vs base; hiring buffer still intact -> recommend small hiring slow-down (pause noncritical infra hire in Sprint 9).
- Downside B (-25% price): revenue delta -$560k ARR vs base; cash buffer stress: triggers hiring freeze from Sprint 7 onward unless slug of Dedicated contract converts. Suggest temporary redirection of 2 hires to contract support (reduce payroll burn by ~ $140k annualized).
- Upside (+10% price): revenue delta +$230k ARR vs base; comfortably supports hiring plan and extra $100k for burst-reserve prepayments (improves margin on token-heavy features).

Key levers to manage sensitivity risk (operational playbook):
1) Rapid SKU pricing toggles: be able to adjust public price band for new accounts within 48h and send negotiated credit to early customers when rolling price up.
2) Hiring sequencing: prioritize inference-engineering hires earlier (Sprint 1-3) as they directly drive quality/cost improvements (quantization/latency) that recover margin.
3) Burst reserve prepay: shift 25% of forecasted burst spend to prepay at Sprint 6 for discounted rate; this yields effective ~9% gross cost reduction for burst tokens.
4) Dedicated sales acceleration: prioritize 1 enterprise pilot (expected ARR $420k/year) to cover 30% of incremental payroll if secured before Sprint 8.
5) Contractor flex: keep two senior infra contractors as stop-gap to avoid full FTE offers until price environment stabilizes.

Spreadsheet formulas (documented so engineering can reproduce):
- per_sprint_cost(role) = (annual_full_loaded_cost(role) / 26) * hire_ramp_factor (ramp 0.3 first sprint -> 0.6 second -> 1.0 third).
- incremental_revenue_delta = baseline_tokens_this_sprint * (new_price - baseline_price) / 1000.
- cash_buffer_usage_rate = sum(next_6_sprints_incremental_payroll) / available_hiring_buffer. Trigger if > 0.20.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate actual committed discount for Dedicated with infra team (assumed 18% baseline). (TODO assigned: Dinesh, due 2026-11-20).
- Confirm average token mix (short vs long sequences) with Research to refine per-token compute cost (affects price elasticity mapping). (TODO: Marta).
- Add a rapid scenario that models immediate 40% usage surge from a single PLG event (we currently model only steady growth). (Nathan to prototype).
- Map hiring LOCs to actual recruiting pipeline (are offers queued for Sprint 1-3?) (Riley to sync with TA).

Notes/Working thoughts: this sheet intentionally over-weights inference hires early because we believe product improvements (KV cache, quantization) in Q1 will unlock both cost reduction and improved throughput, which helps hedge against price compression. The runbook action threshold is conservative — we err on pausing hiring rather than pulling forward layoffs.

Quick references:
- Cost model repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models/pull/78 (contains per-arch kernel cost estimates)
- Dedicated discount discussion thread: #sales-pricing (Slack link internal)
- Confluence draft for public pricing bands: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRICING/Public+SKU+Bands

If you're reviewing: please check the per-FTE blended rates (I used current payroll exports but rounded), confirm sprint dates if your team prefers month-based buckets, and flag any immediate enterprise pilots that should be assumed as converted in the Downside B mitigation plan.

Quick change log (working):

- 2026-11-09 replaced naive annualized costs with full-loaded blends, updated ramp assumptions
- 2026-11-13 added burst-prepay lever and updated sensitivity deltas

-- end of sheet --
